On the other hand, real economic convergence is a long-term result and not a condition before a monetary union. In speaking of the euro, there is no need to forget the political element. The euro is, above all, a political operation and does not mean a improvement in the Single Market. European monetary integration is not understood outside the context of European integration. However, I am moved to say that a lasting monetary union requires political cement and that political power is also an element of international monetary importance. One of the major differences between the euro and the other international currencies is that the European currency is not denationalised or supranationalized. But it can also have other consequences related to its use as an international reserve currency, to the extent that the public can have less confidence in a currency which, in addition to the guarantee of an independent central bank, has the support of a strong political power.
